speaker: Doctor
text:
Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Please describe when you first noticed your double vision, difficulty climbing stairs, and upper limb weakness, and if these symptoms are getting worse over time.

REQUEST TEST: CBC, CMP, TSH, Vitamin B12, CK, ESR, CRP.
REQUEST IMAGES: MRI Brain, MRI Cervical Spine, EMG/NCS.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Acetylcholine_Receptor_Antibodies: Present (elevated); Electromyography Findings: Decreased muscle response with repetitive stimulation; Chest_CT Findings: Normal, no thymoma or other masses detected. CBC: NORMAL READINGS; CMP: NORMAL READINGS; TSH: NORMAL READINGS; Vitamin B12: NORMAL READINGS; CK: NORMAL READINGS; ESR: NORMAL READINGS; CRP: NORMAL READINGS. MRI Brain: NORMAL READINGS; MRI Cervical Spine: NORMAL READINGS; EMG/NCS: See Electromyography Findings above.

speaker: Doctor
text: The test results are highly suggestive of Myasthenia Gravis, given the elevated acetylcholine receptor antibodies and the specific EMG findings of decreased muscle response. To confirm the diagnosis and assess the extent of your condition, do you experience any ptosis (drooping eyelids) or worsening of these symptoms toward the end of the day? Additionally, do you have a history of difficulty swallowing or speaking clearly?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis. The combination of elevated acetylcholine receptor antibodies, characteristic EMG findings, and the specific pattern of fluctuating weakness (worsening with activity, improving with rest) confirms the diagnosis.
